content:
Here is a line-by-line English translation. Bracketed words mark damaged or uncertain portions reflected in your text.

1. In those distant days, when day had been fashioned from heaven and earth,
2. in those distant nights, when night had been fashioned from heaven and earth,
3. in those distant years, when names and destinies had been fixed,
4. when the Anuna gods had been born together,
5. when the spouse of Inana had acquired awe-inspiring radiance,
6. when the spouse of Inana had made heaven and earth tremble,
7. when the spouse of Inana […] had grown robust and was ready for begetting,
8. when the gods of the cities had been bound to their cult-seats [and shrines],
9. when the great gods were setting in order their own possessions, and the small gods were lifting the brick-moulds,
10. when the river-gods were kneading the clay, mixing the silt with ḫarali-bitumen,
11. when the wind-gods were roaring and setting in place life and the word,
12. on that day broad understanding and skill abounded; the many great gods were present,
13. Enki was in the engur, the deep, where the flood-waters surge—a place whose heart no god knows by night;
14. on his couch he lay down; he did not get up,
15. the gods cried out again and again; they raised a lament,
16. as for the man who had been laid down to sleep—his resting-place would not let him rise,
17. Namma, the mother-womb who bore the great gods,
18. addressed her children, the weeping gods:
19. she had them sit down before her, and she had them [bow/keep still],
20. [saying:] “Do not rise up …,”
21. “Let the creatures, the work of your hands, make the yoke sweet upon their necks.”
